verifications.claim: The Artemis II Orion capsule re-entered Earth's atmosphere on Friday, April 10, 2026.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'As their spacecraft slipped into Earth’s atmosphere ... on Friday'; R2: '7:53 p.m.: When Orion reaches 400,000 feet ...'; R3: '7:53 p.m. The Orion spacecraft reached Earth’s atmosphere ... on Friday, April 10'
verifications.reasoning: Multiple sources directly confirm re-entry on Friday, April 10, 2026, at entry interface around 7:53 p.m. ET.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II Orion capsule splashed down in the Pacific Ocean west of San Diego on Friday, April 10, 2026, at 8:07 p.m. ET.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'splashdown, at 8:07 p.m. Eastern time ... waters off San Diego'; R2: 'Splashdown ... 8:07 p.m. EDT ... off the coast of San Diego'; R3: 'SPLASHDOWN! ... Pacific Ocean off the coast of San Diego at 8:07 p.m. EDT'
verifications.reasoning: Exact date, time, location (Pacific off San Diego) confirmed across all sources.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II Orion capsule separated from its service module at 7:33 p.m. ET on April 10, 2026.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'At 7:33 p.m. the Orion crew capsule ... detached from the cylindrical service module'; R2: '7:33 p.m.: Orion’s crew module will separate'; R3: '7:33 p.m. Orion’s crew and service module have separated'
verifications.reasoning: Precise time and event directly stated in multiple NASA and news sources.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II Orion capsule hit the upper atmosphere at 7:53 p.m. ET on April 10, 2026.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'At 7:53 p.m., at an altitude of 400,000 feet, it hit ... “entry interface”'; R2: '7:53 p.m.: When Orion reaches 400,000 feet'; R3: '7:53 p.m. The Orion spacecraft reached Earth’s atmosphere 400,000 feet'
verifications.reasoning: Exact time for 'entry interface' (hitting upper atmosphere at 400,000 feet) matches precisely.

verifications.claim: The re-entry initiated a six-minute communications blackout before landing.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'blackout of radio communications for six minutes'; R2: 'planned six-minute communications blackout'; R3: 'planned communications blackout expected to last about six minutes'
verifications.reasoning: All sources confirm exactly six-minute blackout starting at re-entry.

verifications.claim: Drogue parachutes deployed at 8:03 p.m. ET on April 10, 2026 during the Artemis II return.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R2: '8:03 p.m.: ... the drogue parachutes will deploy'; R3: '8:03 p.m. ... the drogue parachutes on Orion deployed'
verifications.reasoning: Precise time for drogue parachute deployment directly matches in NASA sources.

verifications.claim: The crew was safely recovered from the Artemis II Orion capsule by NASA and U.S. Navy teams.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'recovery team ... helped the astronauts out'; R2: 'teams from NASA and the U.S. military will extract the crew'; R3: 'team members from the agency and the U.S. military ... safely extracted'
verifications.reasoning: Multiple sources confirm safe recovery by NASA and U.S. Navy/military teams.

verifications.claim: The crew was transported to the USS John P. Murtha.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'take them to the U.S.S. John P. Murtha'; R2: 'fly them ... to the USS John P. Murtha'; R3: 'flown to the USS John P. Murtha'
verifications.reasoning: All recovery descriptions specify transport to USS John P. Murtha.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II reentry concludes a nearly 10-day mission around the Moon.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'launched ... April 1 ... Friday [April 10]'; R3: 'approximate 10-day mission around the Moon'; R6: 'ending the record-breaking 10-day mission'
verifications.reasoning: Launch April 1 to splashdown April 10 is nearly 10 days; sources explicitly state ~10-day mission.

verifications.claim: Artemis II is the first human-crewed mission to re-enter from lunar distances in over 50 years.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'first people to leave low-Earth orbit since 1972'; R2: 'first humans toward the Moon since 1972'; R4: 'first humans to travel to the moon and return ... since Apollo 17 ... 1972'
verifications.reasoning: Sources confirm first crewed deep space (lunar) mission/re-entry since 1972 (over 50 years in 2026).
